709461.t: From Proto-Hellenic *odónts, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃dónts (“tooth”). Cognates include Sanskrit दत् (dát), Latin dēns and Old English tōþ (English tooth).

709415.t: From earlier ξένϝος (xénwos), from Proto-Hellenic *ksénwos, which Beekes tentatively considers Pre-Greek; he also mentions attempts to connect the term to Proto-Indo-European *gʰóstis (“guest”).

709421.t: From Proto-Indo-European *kseros (“dry”). Cognates include Latin serescō, Old High German serawēn, Old Armenian չոր (čʻor), Middle Armenian չիր (čʻir), and perhaps Sanskrit क्षार (kṣārá, “sharp, acrid, pungent”).

709407.t: Unknown. There are at least two possibilities: # Derived from Proto-Indo-European, through augmented *ḱsendʰ-, from root *ḱas- (“white, blond, grey”).

709458.t: From Proto-Hellenic *hodós, possibly from a Proto-Indo-European *sodós (“course”), which is traditionally derived from *sed- (“to sit”) and directly cognate with Proto-Slavic *xodъ (“motion; passage”), with more distant cognates including Sanskrit सा॒द…

709423.t: Already in Late Mycenaean Greek (Ta-716 from Pylos), attested in the dual 𐀥𐀯𐀟𐀁 (qi-si-pe-e, “two swords”) (mostly ideographically as 𐃉).

709484.t: From Proto-Hellenic *ód͏̌d͏̌ō, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃ed-ye-, from *h₃ed-. Cognates include Latin odor and Lithuanian úosti.

709481.t: From Proto-Hellenic *ózdos, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃ósdos (“branch, twig”). Cognate with Old Armenian ոստ (ost, “branch; knot (of tree)”), Old English ōst (“tree knot”).

709442.t: From Proto-Indo-European *oktōḱomt, from earlier *oḱto(w)-dḱomt (“eight-ten”), influenced by ὀγδόη (ogdóē) in analogy with ἑβδομήκοντα (hebdomḗkonta). Cognate with Latin octōgintā, Old Armenian ութսուն (utʻsun).

709491.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₂oyHseh₂ (“shaft”) or similar. Cognates include Sanskrit ईषा (īṣā́) and Hittite 𒄭𒅖𒊭𒀭 (ḫi-iš-ša-an).

709427.t: Seemingly from a Proto-Indo-European *ksewlo-, which is traditionally derived from Proto-Indo-European *kes- (“to scrape; to comb”) or from *ḱes- (“to cut”), and compared with Lithuanian šùlas (“post; pole; stave”), Russian шу́ло (šúlo, “garden-pole”)…

709433.t: From Proto-Indo-European *ksu-ró-s (“razor”), from *ksew- (“to scrape, sharpen, shave”). Exact cognate with Proto-Indo-Iranian *kšurás (“dagger, razor”); see also the verbal formation from the same root ξύω (xúō, “to scrape”).

709435.t: From Proto-Hellenic *ksuyō, from Proto-Indo-European *ksuyéti, from *ksew- (“to scrape, shave, scratch”). Cognate with Latin novācula, saucius, and many others.

709444.t: Ordinal of ὀκτώ (oktṓ, “eight”). The term derives from earlier *ὄγδοϝος (*ógdowos), itself perhaps from earlier Proto-Indo-European *oḱtṓwos, from Proto-Indo-European *oḱtṓw.

709492.t: From Proto-Indo-European *wóyde (“to have seen; to know”), from *weyd- (“to see; to know”). Compare εἶδον (eîdon, “to see”) and εἴδομαι (eídomai, “to seem”), which originate from different aspectual forms of the same verbal root.

709463.t: From Proto-Indo-European *Hed-ún-eh₂ (“pain”), traditionally derived further from *h₁ed- (“to eat”), and compared with Albanian dhunë (“violence, use of force; damage, injury”), Old Armenian երկն (erkn, “birth pangs”), and Old Irish idu (“pains, birth…

709466.t: Perhaps from the same root as ὀδύνη (odúnē, “pain”).

709434.t: From the root of ξύω (xúō, “to scrape, plane”) + -τός (-tós, adjectival suffix).

709443.t: From ὀγδοήκοντα (ogdoḗkonta, “eighty”) + -στός (-stós), a variant of -τός (-tós, ordinal suffix).

709494.t: From οἰκεῖος (oikeîos, “familial, related; familiar, intimate”) + -της (-tēs, abstract noun suffix).
